classification.result: eligible primary football study; not american_data
classification.rationale: Pac-12 HAP/CAP is a conference-specific registry across Pac-12 institutions, not U.S. High School RIO, the NCAA Injury Surveillance Program, or national U.S. surveillance. The source explicitly distinguishes its Pac-12 athlete-year analysis from prior NCAA athlete-exposure studies and reports a clean women's soccer subgroup.
classification.sourceType: Pac-12 Health Analytics Program/CARE-Affiliated Program conference sports-injury registry

intentionalBlanksAndCaveats: Soccer athlete-years were not printed and were not back-calculated from the count and rate.
The printed 14,486 athlete-years and 815 unique athletes are all-sport totals and were not copied to the soccer subgroup.
The exact soccer team count, soccer-specific player count, and soccer-specific age were not reported; the source only establishes that soccer had more than 5 represented teams.
The contact-class Figure pools multiple sports and was not mapped to soccer.
Soccer-specific illness, severity, recurrence, mechanism, location, burden, match/training, and time-loss metrics were absent; the authors state that concussion mechanism was not directly assessed.
